literal: The strength of the action, and one's own strength, and the strength of the adversary, and the strength of the ally, having weighed, act.
translation: Weigh well the strength of the deed, your own strength, the strength of your adversary, and the strength of your allies, and then act.
modern: ஒரு செயலைச் செய்வதற்கு முன், அச்செயலின் வலிமை, தன் வலிமை, பகைவனின் வலிமை, மற்றும் துணையாக இருப்பவரின் வலிமை ஆகியவற்றை ஆராய்ந்து பார்த்து அச்செயலைச் செய்ய வேண்டும்.
explanation: This couplet outlines the four essential types of strength that must be evaluated before embarking on any major undertaking. First, one must understand the difficulty of the task itself (vinai vali). Second, one must assess their own capabilities and resources (tan vali). Third, the power of the opponent or obstacles must be gauged (māṟṟāṉ vali). Fourth, the strength of one's supporters or allies must be factored in (tuṇai vali). Only after carefully weighing (tūkki) these four elements should one proceed to act (ceyal).
